title: rorca-ensure-postgres

userStories.title: Platform detection and Postgres binary download
userStories.description: Implement the platform detection logic and binary download function in bin/rorca.ts. Detect the current OS/arch combination (darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, win32-x64) and download the correct Postgres 16 binary archive from the zonkyio/embedded-postgres-binaries GitHub releases. Use only Node.js built-ins (https, fs, os, path, child_process). Show a spinner with download progress bytes. Store a version marker at ~/.rorca/postgres/.version after successful download. Skip download if .version file already exists with matching version.
acceptanceCriteria: Platform detection returns one of: darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, win32-x64 — throws a clear error for unsupported platforms (e.g. linux-arm32)
Download function uses Node.js https module to fetch the .tar.gz archive from https://github.com/zonkyio/embedded-postgres-binaries/releases — no npm dependencies added to bin/rorca.ts
Spinner displays during download showing bytes downloaded (e.g. 'Downloading Postgres 16... 42.3 MB / 87.1 MB') using process.stdout.write with \r to overwrite the line
After successful download and extraction, ~/.rorca/postgres/.version file is written containing the version string (e.g. '16.2.0')
If ~/.rorca/postgres/.version already exists with the correct version string, the entire download and extraction is skipped with a log line 'Postgres 16 already installed'

suggestedSkills.name: logging-fundamentals
suggestedSkills.reason: Progress feedback during download requires structured stdout writes and spinner logic

userStories.title: Extract archive and run initdb to initialize data directory
userStories.description: After the binary archive is downloaded to a temp path, extract the .tar.gz to ~/.rorca/postgres/bin/ using Node.js child_process (tar command on unix, expand/7z on windows or tar which ships with Windows 10+). Then run initdb to initialize a fresh data directory at ~/.rorca/postgres/data/ — but ONLY if the data directory does not already exist (idempotent). Pass --no-locale --encoding=UTF8 --username=rorca flags to initdb. Log each step clearly.
acceptanceCriteria: Extraction places postgres binaries at ~/.rorca/postgres/bin/postgres, ~/.rorca/postgres/bin/initdb, ~/.rorca/postgres/bin/pg_ctl, and ~/.rorca/postgres/bin/createuser — verified by checking file existence after extraction
initdb is only called when ~/.rorca/postgres/data/ does not exist — calling ensurePostgres() twice does not re-run initdb or produce an error
initdb is called with --no-locale --encoding=UTF8 --username=rorca — the data directory is owned by the current OS user
If initdb exits with non-zero, ensurePostgres() throws an Error with the stderr output included in the message
Extraction works on macOS (darwin), Linux, and Windows — uses `tar -xzf` on unix, `tar -xzf` on Windows 10+ (tar ships with Windows 10)

suggestedSkills.name: assumption-buster
suggestedSkills.reason: Many implicit assumptions about tar availability, file permissions, and initdb flags need to be challenged and verified across platforms

userStories.title: Start postgres process on port 5433 and create rorca user/database
userStories.description: Start the managed Postgres process using pg_ctl start -D ~/.rorca/postgres/data -o '-p 5433 -k /tmp' and wait until it accepts connections (poll pg_isready or attempt a TCP connect in a loop with 100ms delay, max 30s). After confirming Postgres is up, use psql or createuser/createdb binaries to create the rorca user (if not exists) and rorca database (if not exists). Handle the case where Postgres is already running on 5433 (idempotent: skip start, still ensure user/db exist).
acceptanceCriteria: pg_ctl start is invoked with -D ~/.rorca/postgres/data -o '-p 5433' — the process is started in the background (not blocking the Node process)

After spawning pg_ctl, ensurePostgres() polls for readiness by attempting TCP connect to localhost:5433 every 100ms for up to 30 seconds — throws Error('Postgres failed to start within 30s') if not ready
If port 5433 is already accepting connections before pg_ctl is called, pg_ctl start is skipped entirely (idempotent) — a log line 'Postgres already running on 5433' is shown
createuser -h localhost -p 5433 -s rorca is run; if exit code is non-zero AND stderr contains 'already exists', the error is swallowed (idempotent) — any other non-zero exit throws
createdb -h localhost -p 5433 -O rorca rorca is run with the same idempotent error-swallowing logic for 'already exists'

suggestedSkills.name: distributed-tracing-logs
suggestedSkills.reason: Correlation of startup events and readiness polling steps benefits from structured log context

userStories.title: Wire ensurePostgres() into bin/rorca.ts start command with graceful shutdown
userStories.description: Replace the current lines 147-157 in bin/rorca.ts (which exit with 'Run: docker compose up -d db' if Postgres is unreachable) with a call to ensurePostgres(). Set process.env.DATABASE_URL = 'postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5433/rorca' after ensurePostgres() succeeds. Register SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers that call pg_ctl stop -D ~/.rorca/postgres/data -m fast before process.exit(0) — but only if ensurePostgres() started the managed instance (not if DATABASE_URL was already set by the user). If DATABASE_URL is already set and Postgres is reachable, skip ensurePostgres() entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: When DATABASE_URL env var is set and the target Postgres is reachable (TCP connect succeeds), ensurePostgres() is skipped entirely — no download, no pg_ctl, no init — existing user-provided database is used as-is
When DATABASE_URL is not set, ensurePostgres() runs the full provisioning flow and sets process.env.DATABASE_URL = 'postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5433/rorca' before the Express server starts
SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers call `pg_ctl stop -D ~/.rorca/postgres/data -m fast` only when the managed Postgres was started by ensurePostgres() — a boolean flag `managedPostgresStarted` tracks this
The old docker compose exit message (lines 147-157) is removed — running `rorca start` with no DATABASE_URL no longer prints 'Run: docker compose up -d db'
Graceful shutdown sequence: pg_ctl stop completes before process.exit(0) — the stop command is awaited via execSync or spawnSync to ensure clean shutdown

suggestedSkills.name: logging-fundamentals
suggestedSkills.reason: Clear startup and shutdown log messages improve operational visibility of the ensurePostgres flow

userStories.title: Error handling, edge cases, and manual test of full zero-prereq startup
userStories.description: Harden ensurePostgres() with proper error handling for all failure modes: disk full during download, network timeout, extraction failure, initdb failure, pg_ctl start failure, and port 5453 already in use by a non-Postgres process. Add a --no-postgres flag to rorca start that skips ensurePostgres() and preserves the old behavior (requires user-provided DATABASE_URL). Verify the full flow works end-to-end by running rorca start on a clean machine (no DATABASE_URL, no existing ~/.rorca/postgres/) and confirming Express starts successfully with migrations applied.
acceptanceCriteria: Network timeout during download (>60s with no data) throws Error('Postgres download timed out') and cleans up the partial temp file

If ~/.rorca/postgres/bin/ exists but is missing expected binaries (postgres, initdb, pg_ctl), ensurePostgres() throws Error('Postgres install appears corrupt — delete ~/.rorca/postgres and retry') with actionable user guidance
rorca start --no-postgres skips ensurePostgres() entirely, requires DATABASE_URL to be set, and exits with code 1 + message 'DATABASE_URL required when --no-postgres is set' if it is not

When port 5453 is already bound by a non-Postgres process, pg_ctl start fails — ensurePostgres() detects this (non-zero exit + 'address already in use' in stderr) and throws Error('Port 5453 is already in use by another process') with suggestion to kill the conflicting process

Full zero-prereq test: after deleting ~/.rorca/postgres/, running `rorca start` downloads Postgres, runs initdb, starts on 5433, creates rorca user/db, sets DATABASE_URL, runs migrations, and Express is reachable on :3030 within 90 seconds

suggestedSkills.name: assumption-buster
suggestedSkills.reason: Explicitly tests implicit assumptions: tar availability, disk space, port conflicts, and corrupt installs — assumption-buster methodology drives the edge case list

suggestedSkills.name: redteam
suggestedSkills.reason: Attacker perspective surfaces additional failure modes: symlink attacks on ~/.rorca/postgres/, TOCTOU on .version file, malicious binary substitution during download

contextUsed.text:
=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
Implement ensurePostgres() auto-provisioning in bin/rorca.ts so that rorca start works out of the box with zero prerequisites — no Docker, no manual Postgres install.

Current state: bin/rorca.ts line 147-157 checks if Postgres is reachable and exits with Run: docker compose up -d db if not reachable. This is a blocker for end-user distribution.

Target state: When DATABASE_URL is not set OR Postgres is not reachable, ensurePostgres() should:
1. Check ~/.rorca/postgres/ for an existing managed Postgres install
2. If not present, download the correct platform-specific Postgres 16 binary archive from https://github.com/zonkyio/embedded-postgres-binaries (same source Prisma uses). Platforms: darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, win32-x64.
3. Extract to ~/.rorca/postgres/bin/
4. Run initdb to initialize a data directory at ~/.rorca/postgres/data/ (only on first run)
5. Start the postgres process on port 5433 (not 5432 to avoid conflicts)
6. Create the rorca user and rorca database if they do not exist
7. Set DATABASE_URL=postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5433/rorca in the environment before starting Express
8. On rorca start shutdown (SIGINT/SIGTERM), gracefully stop the managed postgres process

Key constraints:
- Use Node.js built-ins only (https, fs, child_process, path, os) — no new npm dependencies in bin/rorca.ts
- Show clear progress with spinner during download
- Idempotent: if postgres is already running on 5433, skip download/init and just use it
- If DATABASE_URL already points to reachable postgres, skip ensurePostgres entirely
- Store version marker at ~/.rorca/postgres/.version
- pgvector and AGE are NOT bundled — migration graceful degradation handles their absence
